diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, if $G$ has a unique fixed-point, then $(\widehat{\mu}_t)_{t\in\N_0}$ converges $\PROB$-almost surely in $\CW_2$ to the Wasserstein barycenter of $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ with weights $w_1,\ldots,w_K$.
However, to the best of our knowledge, sufficient conditions to guarantee the uniqueness of the fixed-point of~$G$ for non-parametric $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ is still an open problem.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and contribution summary promise convergence to the barycenter for the advertised general non-parametric inputs. The theorem only proves that accumulation points are fixed points of $G$; convergence to the barycenter additionally requires uniqueness of that fixed point, which the paper explicitly says is not known for non-parametric inputs.

failure_location.quote: This gives rise to a computationally tractable stochastic fixed-point algorithm which is provably convergent to the 2-Wasserstein barycenter.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the paper must either prove that every relevant fixed point is the barycenter (or otherwise prove direct barycenter convergence) or consistently restrict the advertised guarantee to cases where $G$ has a unique fixed point.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central unconditional convergence guarantee for general continuous non-parametric measures is unsupported; in the stated general regime the output may only be shown to approach the fixed-point set.
issues.title: Unconditional barycenter-convergence claim exceeds the proved conditional result
issues.why_classification: The available repair either requires new central convergence theory or withdraws the advertised guarantee in the general non-parametric regime.

issues.failure_explanation: Weak convergence alone is strictly weaker than convergence in $\CW_2$; convergence of second moments is also required. For example, $(1-n^{-3})\delta_0+n^{-3}\delta_{n^2}$ converges weakly to $\delta_0$ while its second moments diverge, so it does not converge in $\CW_2$.

failure_location.quote: This induces a metric on the space of probability measures with finite second moments that metrizes the weak convergence; see, e.g., \citep[Theorem~6.9]{villani2009optimal}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace both statements by the standard characterization: $\CW_2$ convergence is equivalent to weak convergence together with convergence of second moments.
issues.overall_effect: The paper twice misstates the topology induced by $\CW_2$. The later precompactness argument can still use the stronger $\CW_2$ convergence already established for the relevant marginals.
issues.title: The Wasserstein metric is incorrectly said to metrize weak convergence alone
issues.why_classification: A short local qualification corrects the statements without changing any substantive theorem or guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The convergence theorem requires truncation indices and sample sizes defined through existence thresholds depending on the full, iteration-dependent measures and, for the entropic estimator, unspecified rate constants. The paper supplies no procedure for computing these thresholds from its sampling access assumptions. The tractability remark only explains how to sample after these quantities have already been chosen, so it does not establish that the convergent configuration is implementable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must give computable or data-driven choices of the truncation radii, sample sizes, and regularization parameters and prove that they satisfy the summable error bounds used in the convergence theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The source separately supports a mathematically convergent oracle configuration and tractable finite operations for user-chosen parameters, but not a single computationally tractable algorithm carrying the proved convergence guarantee.
issues.title: The provably convergent parameter choices are not shown computationally obtainable
issues.why_classification: Making the convergence-enforcing choices executable requires new constructive bounds or an adaptive convergence argument; otherwise the central combined tractability-and-convergence promise must be withdrawn.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition states its consistency bound for every $m\ge1$ and $n\ge d+1$, but the invoked estimate is only stated in the proof for $m,n\ge2$, and the simplified bound actually used is established only for $m,n\ge7$. No argument covers the omitted small-sample cases; in particular, the displayed $m=1$ term contains $\log(1)=0$ and cannot represent the error caused by having only one source sample.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the risk bound to $m,n\ge7$ and set the admissible estimator's lower sample-size constants accordingly, or supply separate valid bounds for the finitely many smaller sample sizes.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-sample scope of the displayed risk guarantee is overstated. The asymptotic consistency and convergence construction use thresholds at least seven and therefore can survive a restricted sample-size statement.
issues.title: Entropic-estimator risk bound is claimed for sample sizes not covered by the proof
issues.why_classification: Restricting the bound to the range actually proved is a local repair and preserves the estimator's consistency and all asymptotic convergence guarantees.
